newsitem.title: USA: Russian says Yeltsin in charge but not full-speed.
newsitem.headline: Russian says Yeltsin in charge but not full-speed.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday President Boris Yeltsin is well enough to oversee "all the necessary issues" but is not well enough yet to be working full-time.

"The president is not able to be constantly in the office now. He's not in good enough health for this," Chernomyrdin said through a Russian interpreter at a joint news conference with U.S. Vice President Al Gore. But he added, "The president is recovering and he oversees all the necessary issues."

Chernomyrdin was asked whether Yeltsin -- who is recovering from heart bypass surgery and pneumonia -- was "focussed" and truly in charge of matters in Russia, as he and Gore fielded questions upon conclusion of a two-day meeting of a U.S.-Russia liaison group.

They signed a number of economic and technical agreements and pronounced the meeting a success. But what made the state of Yeltsin's health especially topical was that they also announced earlier on Friday that a planned March 20-21 summit meeting between the Russian and U.S. President Bill Clinton would be shifted to Helsinki, a site much more convenient to the ailing Yelstin than the United States.

Chernomyrdin said it was too much to expect that a man who had suffered the double physical blow Yeltsin had sustained would be back to full speed so soon. But he maintained Yeltsin nonetheless remained in political control.

"The president is active both politically, he meets at the highest level and he does everything that he has to do in the country," Chernomyrdin said. "He talks over the telephone. He is working, but he needs some time to completely recover."
